summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator, a private investigator, breaks through a second-story window by tearing its bars out of the wall and crashing into a room full of armed hostiles. Using leverage, momentum, and improvised weapons, she takes down four attackers, including a female shooter and a boy whom she hits with a glass shard, and a plant-slingshot throw defeats the last gunman. Afterward she checks on Tresting, an ex-cop who has a graze on his right bicep, while he struggles with shock and stares at the scene. The narrator, who enjoys impressing people, acknowledges her own bleeding and her acute awareness of her body.
one_line: A private investigator smashes through a second-story window, defeats four armed attackers with improvised weapons, and checks on the shaken ex-cop Tresting.
key_facts: The narrator's left foot leveraged against the falling bars kept her from tumbling twenty feet to the pavement.
The narrator smashed her upper body through a naked window, and the blinds came down with her in a shower of broken shards.
The narrator scissored her legs to take down the shooter standing closest to the window, who was not Tresting.
The narrator armed herself with a piece of broken window pane in each hand, and the glass from one hand struck the boy, who dropped his gun and clutched at his throat.
Tresting took cover behind his gun safe while the narrator fought the room's attackers.
The last hostile screamed inarticulately as he brought his Glock around before the narrator dove over the desk.
The narrator grabbed a tall, tree-like houseplant and spun it like a slingshot, so its heavy clay pot struck the last hostile in the face.
Tresting emerged from behind the safe with his Beretta twitching in his hand and stared with wide, unblinking eyes.
Tresting said, "That window's two stories up," and the narrator replied, "That's right."
Tresting touched his right bicep, where blood glistened on his fingertips, and called it a graze.
When Tresting said "It had bars on it," the narrator answered, "Yup. I'm just that good."
The scene contained four bodies, broken glass, and dirt.
Tresting is described as an ex-cop.
The narrator says she has a hyper-awareness of her own body and that all the math in the world won't help if she can't match calculation with reality.
